# ada-url / parse

ada-url's own fuzz target `parse` ([source](source/parse.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over ada (ada-url/ada at e6754478).

Checks 8 properties (listed below); the first, a differential check: For valid-UTF-8 input, parse<url> and parse<url_aggregator> agree on success (also for base-relative parses, where hrefs must also be equal; and for a grammar-generated simple absolute candidate, where hrefs must be equal).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against ada at commit e6754478.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- All ten components (protocol, href, hostname, pathname, search, hash, port, username, password, host) are equal between ada::url and ada::url_aggregator (asserts at 287-304). After set_href(source) on both, ONLY href is compared again (assert at 313), not the other nine components ([lines 287-313](source/parse.cc#L287-L313)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- clear_port/clear_search/clear_hash postconditions: has_x() becomes false and get_x() becomes empty ([lines 450-479](source/parse.cc#L450-L479)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After every step of a fuzz-chosen sequence of up to 8 setters (protocol/username/password/hostname/host/pathname/search/hash/port) applied to both representations, their hrefs are identical ([lines 582-643](source/parse.cc#L582-L643)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Re-parsing the href of a successful url_aggregator parse must succeed and give the identical href ([lines 653-668](source/parse.cc#L653-L668)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- url_search_params serialisation is a fixed point: url_search_params(sp.to_string()).to_string() == sp.to_string() (sp taken from a URL whose query is the fuzz input, plus an appended pair) ([lines 681-708](source/parse.cc#L681-L708)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

A failure of the check at lines 287-313 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name it exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies it on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other checks.
